key_definitions.Management: A process of interrelated functions performed by all managers to effectively and efficiently achieve the goals of an organisation. (Koontz: creating an internal environment where individuals work effectively).
key_definitions.Coordination: The force that binds all the functions of management together. It synchronises activities of different departments towards common goals. It is the ESSENCE of management.
key_definitions.Scientific_Management: Knowing exactly what you want men to do and seeing that they do it in the best and cheapest way. (FW Taylor)
key_definitions.Planning: Deciding in advance what is to be done, when, how and by whom. It bridges the gap between where we are and where we want to go. (ME Hurley: selection among alternatives of policies, procedures and programmes)
key_definitions.Organising: The process of identifying and grouping activities, defining authority-responsibility relationships to achieve organisational goals. (Louis Allen)
key_definitions.Delegation: The downward transfer of authority from a superior to a subordinate to operate within prescribed limits. (Theo Haimann) Authority is delegated; responsibility is never delegated.
key_definitions.Decentralisation: Systematic effort to delegate to the lowest level all authority except that which can only be exercised at central points. (Louis Allen)
key_definitions.Staffing: The process of hiring and developing the required personnel to fill in various positions in the organisation. (Koontz & O'Donnell)
key_definitions.Recruitment: The process of searching for prospective employees and stimulating them to apply for jobs.
key_definitions.Selection: The process of selecting the best candidate from applicants, mainly by interviewing and conducting selection tests.
key_definitions.Training: Activity conducted to increase the skill and knowledge of the person to do a specific job.
key_definitions.Development: Activity that aims for overall growth of the employee beyond the current job.
key_definitions.Directing: Consists of the processes and techniques utilised in issuing instructions and making decisions that operations are carried on as originally planned. (Theo Haimann)
key_definitions.Motivation: A process of stimulating people to action to accomplish desired goals. (William Scott)
key_definitions.Leadership: The activity of influencing people to strive willingly for group objectives. (George Terry)
key_definitions.Communication: The process of passing information and understanding from one person to another.
key_definitions.Controlling: Managerial control implies the measurement of accomplishment against the standard and the correction of deviations to assure attainment of objectives. (Koontz & O'Donnell)
key_definitions.Financial_Management: Area of financial decision-making, harmonising individual motives and enterprise goals. (Weston & Brigham)
key_definitions.Marketing: A social process by which individual groups obtain what they need and want through creating, freely exchanging products and services of value with others. (Philip Kotler)
key_definitions.Marketing_Mix: The set of marketing tools that a firm uses to pursue its marketing objectives in the target market — 4Ps: Product, Price, Place, Promotion. (Philip Kotler)
key_definitions.Consumer: Any person who buys any goods for consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised or under any scheme of deferred payment. (CPA 2019)
key_definitions.Business_Environment: The sum total of all individuals, institutions and other forces outside the control of a business enterprise that may affect its performance. (Arthur M Weimer)

key_facts_for_mcq.Financial_incentives: Pay and allowances, Bonus, Profit sharing, Co-partnership, Productivity linked wages, Retirement benefits, Perquisites
key_facts_for_mcq.Non_financial_incentives: Status, Job enrichment, Job security, Employee participation, Organisational climate, Career advancement, Employee recognition, Employee empowerment
key_facts_for_mcq.Grapevine: Informal communication — fast but may be distorted
key_facts_for_mcq.Financial_decisions_3: Investment Decision (capital budgeting), Financing Decision (capital structure), Dividend Decision
key_facts_for_mcq.Promotion_mix_4: Advertising, Personal Selling, Sales Promotion, Public Relations

tips: Q1-Q26 ALL compulsory — never leave any blank. Attempt every question for part marks
Only Q27-Q30 have OR choice — use reading time to decide which option is easier
MCQ traps: 'Coordination is the ESSENCE (not function)'; 'Staffing is responsibility of ALL levels'; 'Money spent on marketing is INVESTMENT not wastage'
FW Taylor = Scientific Management; Henry Fayol = Administrative Management (Modern Management). Do NOT confuse

Fayol's 14 principles: memorise all 14 — Unity of Command, Unity of Direction, Scalar Chain, Division of Work, Authority & Responsibility, Discipline, Subordination of Individual to General Interest, Remuneration, Centralisation, Order, Equity, Stability of Personnel, Initiative, Esprit de Corps
Taylor's 8 foremen: 4 for Planning (Route clerk, Instruction card clerk, Time & Cost clerk, Disciplinarian) + 4 for Execution (Speed boss, Gang boss, Repair boss, Inspector)
Maslow's hierarchy BOTTOM to TOP: Physiological → Safety → Social/Belonging → Esteem → Self-Actualisation
Consumer Protection limits: District ≤ ₹1 crore; State ₹1-10 crore; National > ₹10 crore
Quality marks: ISI = industrial goods; AGMARK = agricultural; FPO = processed food; Hallmark = jewellery
For SA distinction questions: USE TABLE FORMAT — examiners give bonus marks for clarity
For LA: Start with definition, list points with bold headings, end with conclusion or significance
Comparison asked: Fayol vs Taylor; Centralisation vs Decentralisation; Formal vs Informal Org; Training vs Development; Recruitment vs Selection
LPG = Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation — implemented in India in 1991
